title: 2019 Toyota RAV4 Used Car Buyer's Guide: Recalls and Complaints
description: Review the federal record for the 2019 Toyota RAV4: 7 recalls, 873 complaints, and what to check before buying used.

body.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: Before buying a 2019 RAV4, check if all recalls are completed, especially the fuel pump and engine coolant recalls.

body.heading: What the federal record shows
paragraphs: The federal record for the 2019 Toyota RAV4 includes 7 recall campaigns and 873 consumer complaints filed with NHTSA. These are the official and consumer-reported data we have for this model year. We have not driven or tested this vehicle; our analysis is based solely on this record.

The recalls cover a range of components, from fuel system to suspension. The complaints are consumer allegations, not confirmed defects, and they do not indicate a failure rate. Without sales data, we cannot compare complaint totals across models.
bullets: 7 recall campaigns
873 consumer complaints
25 complaints mention a crash, 2 mention a fire, 21 mention injuries

body.heading: Recall campaigns
paragraphs: The 2019 RAV4 has 7 recall campaigns on file. These are official actions by Toyota or its distributors to address safety-related defects or noncompliance. Each recall has a specific remedy, and owners should ensure all are completed.

The recalls include: a fuel pump issue that could cause stalling (20V682000), an engine coolant leak risk (20V064000), a power steering assist loss (20V373000), front lower suspension arm cracks (20V286000), incorrect load capacity labels (19V503000 and 19V244000), and a backup camera malfunction (19V576000).
bullets: Fuel pump: 20V682000 – engine stall risk
Engine coolant: 20V064000 – overheating and fire risk
Power steering: 20V373000 – loss of assist
Suspension arms: 20V286000 – loss of control
Labels: 19V503000 and 19V244000 – incorrect load capacity info
Backup camera: 19V576000 – may not activate in reverse

body.heading: What owners reported
paragraphs: Consumer complaints to NHTSA are allegations, not confirmed defects. They represent what some owners experienced. The most common complaint categories are fuel/propulsion system (254 complaints), engine (211), unknown or other (169), electrical system (101), structure (89), and power train (80).

Examples from the fuel system complaints describe the fuel tank accepting less fuel than expected when the gauge reads empty, reducing driving range. Some owners reported this issue. Engine complaints include a coolant bypass valve failure that could lead to overheating, as reported by some owners. Other complaints mention sunroof glass cracking, electrical display malfunctions, lift gate hinge failures, and transmission problems.

body.heading: What to check before you buy
paragraphs: Before buying a used 2019 RAV4, verify that all recalls have been performed. You can check by VIN on the NHTSA website or at a Toyota dealer. Pay special attention to the fuel pump and engine coolant recalls, as they address stalling and fire risks.

Also, consider the complaints as a guide for a pre-purchase inspection. Have a mechanic check the fuel system for proper fuel gauge accuracy, the engine for coolant leaks, and the power steering for assist function. Inspect the sunroof, lift gate hinges, and electrical components for issues.
bullets: Check recall completion by VIN
Test fuel gauge accuracy and fill-up behavior
Inspect engine for coolant leaks or overheating signs
Verify power steering assist works at low speeds
Examine sunroof glass and lift gate hinges for cracks or wear
Test all electrical displays and controls

body.heading: How we read this
paragraphs: We base this analysis solely on the federal record: recall campaigns and consumer complaints. Recalls are official, but complaints are allegations. We do not have sales data, so we cannot say how common these issues are. We also cannot estimate repair costs or compare this vehicle to others.

Our goal is to give you a clear picture of what the record shows so you can make an informed decision. Use this information to guide your inspection and negotiation, but remember that each used car is unique.

body.heading: Before you make an offer
paragraphs: The 2019 RAV4 has a substantial recall history, but many issues are addressable. Ensure all recalls are done and have a mechanic check the fuel system, engine, and steering. Complaints suggest potential problems, but they are not confirmed defects. With proper inspection, you can mitigate risks and make a sound purchase.
bullets: Verify recall completion. Ensure all 7 recalls, especially fuel pump and engine coolant, are done to avoid stalling or fire risks.
Test fuel gauge accuracy. Fill the tank and see if it accepts more than 9-10 gallons when empty; some owners reported low capacity.
Check for coolant leaks. Inspect engine bay for leaks or signs of overheating, as some owners reported coolant bypass valve failure.
Test power steering. At low speeds, steering should be easy; if not, the EPS gear box may need replacement.
Inspect sunroof and lift gate. Look for cracks in sunroof glass and check lift gate hinges for separation or water leaks.
Test electrical systems. Operate the display, backup camera, and controls to ensure they work consistently.
